comparison: Both evaluations agree that the 1-bp forward stepping (C2, C3) is convincingly supported by high-resolution optical tweezers data. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the evidence as 'convincing' and 'impressive,' matching OpenEval's assessment.

Partial overlap on claims C36, C37, C40 regarding ATP-independence and novelty. OpenEval finds these well-supported, but peer reviewers express concerns about the complex stepping behavior including the characterization of non-1-bp steps, leading to uncertainty.

Both address the 5-bp backsteps and their pairing with forward steps (C4, C43-C46, C48-C49). OpenEval finds the evidence well-supported, but peer reviewers express concerns that 'Figure 4E does not clearly show that the probability of taking 5bp steps depends on ATP concentration,' indicating uncertainty about these complex behaviors.

Perfect agreement on claims C13-C17, C19, C27 regarding XPD's repetitive unwinding behavior, re-annealing characteristics, and low processivity. Both evaluations accept these observations as part of the convincing technical achievements without challenge.
Perfect agreement on claims C28-C35 regarding XPD monomer versus multimer activity and kinetic parameters. Both evaluations accept these experimental findings without raising concerns.

Both address sequence dependence and the passive unwinding mechanism (C5, C50-C58, C70). OpenEval finds strong support with good model fits and independent validation. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting that 'the analyzed data in Figure 6 are rather scattered and many fits appear to be poor,' questioning the quality of evidence.

Perfect agreement on claims C41, C42, C47 regarding 1-bp stepping kinetics, ATP-dependence, and Michaelis-Menten behavior. Peer reviewers do not challenge these characterizations, focusing their concerns elsewhere.

Both address the proposed structural mechanism for 5-bp backsteps involving a secondary DNA binding site (C61, C63-C67). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging it as a plausible but unvalidated model. Peer reviewers are more critical, explicitly stating 'The suggestion that this is due to DNA release from a secondary site on the helicase has not been substantiated' and suggesting alternative mechanisms should be considered.

Both address speculative claims about biological function and broader implications (C72-C75). OpenEval acknowledges these extend beyond experimental data but are appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers note that 'a satisfying biological explanation been provided' has not been achieved, indicating shared uncertainty about functional interpretations.

Partial overlap on broader mechanistic generalizations (C6, C76, C81). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature extending beyond data. Peer reviewers do not challenge these generalizations about applicability to other helicases, focusing concerns on specific XPD mechanism details instead.

OpenEval evaluates claims C18, C22-C26 regarding ruling out alternative mechanisms (opposite-strand translocation, looping). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these comparative analyses were not explicitly addressed in peer comments.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1, C7-C12, C38, C59-C60, C78-C80 representing established literature knowledge and characterization of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not comment on these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim C71 as a mathematical consequence of the kinetic model (v=0 when kF=kR). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this logical derivation was not explicitly addressed by peer reviewers.
